COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.951 of 2024
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. A.S. Rawat, learned Senior Advocate assisted
by Mr. Girveer Chand, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Additional Chief
Standing Counsel for the State.
3. Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for respondent
no.2.
4. The case of the petitioner in a nutshell is that
pursuant to an advertisement issued by the respondent-Public Service Commission for the post of Operator,
petitioner submitted his candidature. Petitioner submitted
his candidature under the Schedule Caste Category. He
got selected and his name found place at Sr. No.2 in the
Select/Merit List.
5. Learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner
contends that there are only one post available under the
SC Category and the person-Suraj Kumar Gautam who
has been selected and found place at Sr. No.1 of the
Select/Merit List does not want to join the service with
the respondent-Public Service Commission, as he has
already joined in Forest Department.
6. It is on this premise, the present writ petition has
been filed by the petitioner seeking a direction to the
respondent for permitting him to join the post in place of
the person-Suraj Kumar Gautam, whose name is in the
Select List at Sr. No.1 in the S.C. Category.
7. This Court vide order dated 14.06.2024 directed

2
learned counsel for respondent no.2-Commission to seek
clear instructions in the matter that as to whether any
recommendations have been made to the department or
any appointment letter is issued to any person or not.
8. Learned counsel for the Commission submitted
that he has no clear instructions, however he further
submits that before appointment letter have been issued to
the person at Sr. No.1, he cannot relinquish his right to
the post. Until and unless the S.C. Candidate, who is at
Sr. No.1 is selected and appointed and relinquished his
right, no such offer can be made to the petitioner.
9. I have considered rival submission made by the
learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10. This Court is of the opinion that the writ petition is
bereft of merit simply for the reason that no
recommendation has been made and appointment has not
been given to any of the person in the select list,
therefore, there is no question of relinquishment arises in
the matter. Moreover the petitioner has nowhere stated in
the writ petition that appointment has been offered to the
selected candidate.
11. Accordingly, writ petition is dismissed in limine.
12. However petitioner is at liberty to file a writ
petition as and when cause of action arises.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 21.06.2024
